newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian car data shortfall due to reexports-Ford.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian car data shortfall due to reexports-Ford.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said on Monday the discrepancy between the registrations and sales of its new cars in Hungary was due mainly to a Hungarian customer re-selling cars abroad.

Ford was responding to claims by Opel Southeast Europe Ltd (OSE), a unit of General Motors Corp's German automaker Adam Opel AG, that the difference between Ford's registrations and sales was the largest in Hungary among all automakers this year.
OSE said on Monday that in this year's first quarter, Ford reported 1,349 new car sales, while Hungary's Ministry of Interior recorded only 574 new registrations of Ford cars.
"This was mainly due to a Ford dealer selling cars to a Hungarian company that re-exported the cars," a Ford spokesman in Budapest told Reuters.
"This practice is not compatible with Ford's policy...of not selling cars to companies that re-export them, so Ford has forbidden this practice," the spokesman said.

Ford stopped dealer sales to re-exporters last year, but the discrepancy in the data continues to appear as the re-exporter was in the first quarter still taking delivery of cars ordered before the policy took effect, the spokesman said.
